today.d: October core PCE at 3.3% and Section 301 tariffs on 14 trading partners knocked the S&P 3.2% lower at the open, but dip buyers and a Michael Burry post turned the tape: the Dow closed higher, eight of 11 sectors rose and the equal-weight ETF beat SPY by 1.12 points.
today.c1: The S&P 500 fell as much as 3.2% within the first half hour, then closed 0.25% lower at 7,182.78. The Nasdaq Composite was down 4.6% at its low and finished 0.62% lower at 23,585.80, while the Dow erased a 1,105-point hole to close up 164.25 points at 50,182.95. October core PCE rose 3.3% year over year against a 3.2% forecast, with headline PCE at 3.8% and third-quarter GDP revised up to 4.3%, and the White House proposed Section 301 tariffs on 14 trading partners including China, the EU and Japan. Nvidia was off almost 7% at midday before closing 3.91% lower at $149.30, after S&P Global put its AA rating on CreditWatch Negative; Micron lost 4.53%, Oracle 5.13% and Alphabet 2.13%. The damage stayed narrow: eight of 11 sectors rose, materials +2.07% and real estate +0.92% led, the equal-weight S&P 500 ETF added 0.83% against SPY's -0.29%, and the Russell 2000 gained 0.71%. The VIX traded back above 30 in the morning and settled 7.32% higher at 28.29.
today.c4:
• The trigger: core PCE at 3.3% kept a December hike fully priced, and Section 301 duties on 14 partners added a trade shock on top of the AI de-rating.
  • The reversal: a 1,105-point Dow hole became a 164-point gain, helped by thin pre-holiday volume and Michael Burry's "temporarily almost entirely long" post.
  • The breadth: eight of 11 sectors rose and the equal-weight ETF beat SPY by 1.12 points, so the index loss was a megacap problem.
  • The AI tell: S&P Global put Nvidia's AA rating on CreditWatch Negative and Ambarella fell 19.77% on guidance.
  • The gate: OPEC+ on 11/29, then the December 8-9 FOMC; US markets are closed 11/26 and shut at 1 p.m. ET on 11/27.

chains.t: ① The Morning Priced a Shock, the Afternoon Priced a Holiday Tape
steps: October core PCE rose 3.3% year over year against a 3.2% forecast, with headline PCE at 3.8% and third-quarter GDP revised up to 4.3%, keeping a December hike fully priced.
The White House proposed Section 301 tariffs on 14 trading partners including China, the EU and Japan; China faces 20% on top of the 25% imposed in 2018.
The S&P fell 3.2% and the Nasdaq 4.6% at their lows inside the first half hour, and the Dow was down more than 1,100 points.
Nvidia was off almost 7% at midday before closing 3.91% lower at $149.30.
Buyers returned after midday: traders cited thin pre-Thanksgiving volume and a Michael Burry newsletter saying his portfolio is "temporarily almost entirely long".
The Dow closed up 164.25 points at 50,182.95 and the S&P 0.25% lower, while the VIX settled at 28.29 after trading above 30.
chains.d: The morning was a tariff-and-inflation shock, the afternoon a holiday-tape reversal: the Dow turned a 1,105-point loss into a 164-point gain and the S&P kept less than a tenth of its worst loss.

news.fact: The personal consumption expenditures price index rose 0.3% in October, putting the annual rate at 3.8%, while core PCE increased 3.3% year over year against a 3.2% forecast.
The U.S. proposed a slew of new tariffs on 14 trading partners, including China, the European Union and Japan; China faces a 20% tariff on top of the 25% imposed in 2018.
The Dow lost more than 1,100 points, or 2.2%, at its low, while the S&P 500 shed 3.2% and the Nasdaq 4.6% at theirs.
Nvidia led AI-related stocks lower, dropping almost 4% on the day.
Traders chalked up part of the rebound to light trading ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday and to a blog post by Michael Burry saying his portfolio is temporarily almost entirely long.
The CBOE Volatility Index rose back above 30 in the morning and was last trading at 33.70, after settling at 26.36 on Tuesday.
Nvidia was off almost 7% at midday as the AI sell-off continued.
Nvidia closed at $149.30, down 3.91% from $155.38.
The S&P 500 closed at 7,182.78, down 18.31 points or 0.25% from 7,201.09.

chains.d: The index fell only because its largest stocks did: breadth was positive all session, materials and real estate were bid, and an equal-weighted portfolio beat the cap-weighted one by more than a point.

chains.d: The AI complex lost its rating anchor: S&P put Nvidia's AA rating on watch, memory names kept falling, and even a Dell beat bought only 0.6%.

chains.t: ⑤ Oil Found a War Premium Again
steps: Brent for January settled up $3.21, or 3.51%, at $94.61, and WTI up $1.63, or 2.0%, at $83.68.
The trigger was Houthi claims of attacks on Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery and on Riyadh's financial district.
EIA crude stocks rose 1.1 million barrels to 418.9 million, 3% below the five-year average, with refinery runs at 97.5% of capacity.
Short covering ahead of Thanksgiving and the OPEC+ meeting on 11/29 to set 2027 quotas added to the bid.
Brent is still 16.59% lower for November, so the session's premium sits inside a month-long slide rather than a tightening.
chains.d: Oil's rally was a war premium plus short covering, not a shortage: Brent settled 3.51% higher but is still 16.59% lower this month.

mtd.h: November Is Still -5.24%, With Two Sectors Below -13%
mtd.d: November's damage remains an AI-and-oil story: technology -13.21% and energy -13.02% are the worst of the 11 sectors, the S&P is 5.24% below its 10/30 base, and five sectors are above the line with financials flat.
mtd.c1: November is a 5.24% drawdown on the S&P 500 from the 10/30 base of 7,580.07, and its shape is unchanged: the month's high was 7,688.62 on 11/4, its low 6,910.39 on 11/20, and the rebound since has recovered 272.39 points, 35.0% of the 10.12% slide from that high. Technology (-13.21%) and energy (-13.02%) are the two worst of the 11 sectors; communications +5.49%, staples +3.22%, consumer discretionary +1.83%, real estate +1.60% and utilities +0.41% are above the line, and financials are unchanged. The Nasdaq is 7.28% lower for the month against the Dow's 3.07%, and the S&P is 8.14% below its 10/6 record.
mtd.c4:
• The shape: the 11/20 low was 8.83% below the base; the rebound has taken that to 5.24%.
  • The breadth: five of 11 sectors are above the 10/30 line and financials are flat.
  • The hedge that paid: the VIX is 45.67% higher at 28.29; gold -9.25%, bitcoin -22.10% and Brent -16.59% all lost money, and the 10Y's 9bp decline was worth only about 0.5% in price.
  • The rates: the 2Y rose 5bp while the 10Y fell 9bp, a 14bp flattening to 24bp.
  • The next test: OPEC+ on 11/29, then the December 8-9 FOMC the market has already priced for a hike.

qtd.h: Q4 Is a 6.13% Drawdown the Dow Didn't Have
qtd.d: Q4 has taken the S&P 6.13% below its 9/30 base and the Nasdaq 12.19%, while the 10Y has fallen 44bp: an AI de-rating with a bond rally, not a rate shock.
qtd.c1: Q4 is a 6.13% drawdown on the S&P 500 from the 9/30 base of 7,651.54 and a 12.19% drawdown on the Nasdaq, while the Dow is only 1.42% lower. The quarter's low was 6,910.39 on 11/20, 9.69% below the base; the rebound has recovered 272.39 points, 35.0% of that drawdown. Technology is 20.41% lower for the quarter and communications 5.04% lower, while staples +14.52%, utilities +10.57%, health +9.06% and consumer discretionary +7.95% lead: seven of 11 sectors are higher. The 10Y fell 44bp over the same window, so the de-rating came with a bond bid rather than a rate shock.
qtd.c4:
• The shape: an AI de-rating inside an equity drawdown, with the Dow down only 1.42% against the Nasdaq's 12.19%.
  • The rates: 10Y -44bp, 30Y -40bp and 2Y -27bp; 2s10s flattened 17bp to 24bp.
  • The rotation: seven of 11 sectors are higher, led by staples and utilities.
  • The commodity side: gold -15.49%, bitcoin -28.03% and Brent +0.10% on a roll-adjusted basis.
  • The carry: the 2Y is still 114bp above its 2026 starting point even after this quarter's 27bp give-back.

ytd.h: The Year Is Still Green, but the AI Index Barely Is
ytd.d: 2026 has round-tripped: the S&P is 4.93% above its 12/31 base after being 14.22% higher at the 10/6 record, the Nasdaq is only 1.48% higher, and the 10Y sits 67bp above where the year started.
ytd.c1: 2026 is still a positive year, but barely for the AI index. The S&P 500 is 4.93% above its 12/31 base of 6,845.50 after being 14.22% higher at the 10/6 record of 7,818.93, and it is now 8.14% below that record. The Nasdaq is 1.48% higher after leading the first nine months; energy +36.21%, staples +18.82% and health +18.66% are the year's leaders, while communications -10.48% is the only double-digit loser. The 10Y is 67bp higher at 4.85%, with the 2Y up 114bp, and gold is 18.50% lower: the year's gains survived the quarter, but the leadership rotated.
ytd.c4:
• The round trip: S&P +14.22% at the 10/6 record is now +4.93%, a 9.29-point give-back.
  • The leadership: energy, staples and health replaced AI at the top of the year's return table.
  • The rates: the front end is 114bp higher and the 2s10s spread has flattened from 71bp to 24bp.
  • The stores of value: gold -18.50% and bitcoin -31.28%, the year's worst assets.
  • The base case: the year is positive because earnings and defensives held; AI still adds, with tech +8.21% against the S&P's +4.93%, but it no longer leads.
